messages:
Alex (PM): Hey team — I pushed a PRD draft for 'Scoped tokens & RBAC scope matrix' to Google Drive: https://drive.redwood/prd/scoped-tokens. Need quick prioritization: core asks from enterprise pilots + acceptance criteria. Can folks skim and call out must-haves vs nice-to-haves by EOD? Thanks.

Priya (eng-security): Skimming now. Two constraints to flag: (1) token evaluation must be O(1) per request (no DB roundtrip for every check) — prefer signed scopes in JWT or HMAC envelope, (2) must support key rotation without immediate invalidation of long-lived tokens.

Taylor (solutions): Customer wishlist (collected from 3 pilots): - project-scoped API keys (read/write) - token with limited model access (model-level allowlist) - time-bound session tokens (short TTL with refresh) - audit fields injected in requests. All are high priority for pilots.

Marco (eng-infra): Infra note: for Private deployments we can't rely on central KMS; need a fallback KMS abstraction and a local cache for signing keys. Also need perf numbers; estimating +5-10% latency for token verification if we add sig checks inline.

Jamie (sre): Rollout constraints: feature flags per org, canaries by usage, fallback to legacy API-keys on mismatch. Acceptance criteria should include metrics: error rate <=0.05% and token verification latency p95 < 10ms.

Priya (eng-security): Proposed minimal viable scope (MVS): - org-scoped token (org_id in token) - project-scoped permission claims (projects:[id:role,...]) - role mapping for admin/editor/viewer - token introspection endpoint (for STS/migration). Anything else is nice-to-have.

Alex (PM): MVS sounds right. Need to nail migration story: how do we map existing API keys? Taylor: Customers want seamless rotation: server-side mapping where old API key maps to new scoped token with same perms during a transition window.

Priya (eng-security): Edge cases: - cross-org service accounts? deny by default unless explicitly whitelisted - tokens issued for multiple projects: must be intersection-of-allowed-resources - revocation list scale: store in LRU cache + invalidate via push hook.

Marco (eng-infra): Ops requirement: telemetry fields must include issuing_key_id, org_id, project_ids, role_hash. Also we'll add a "token_version" header to support upgrades.

Alex (PM): Acceptance criteria (draft): 1) token format documented + examples, 2) SDKs support minting and refreshing, 3) canary in hosted with 5 customers, 4) migration tool for mapping existing keys, 5) test matrix covering cross-org, revoked tokens, expired tokens.

Taylor (solutions): Quick example snippet for API call -> `Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci... scope:"org:org123 project:projA=read"` (we should standardize claim names). Add example of error responses.

Priya (eng-security): Security checks: must validate `aud` and `exp`, support `nbf`, and ensure signer uses per-tenant KMS in Private mode. Also add HSM/KMS rotation schedule docs.

Jamie (sre): Who owns rollout runbook? Alex assign to Priya for spec + Marco for infra runway. I'll draft runbook template.

Alex (PM): OK — owners: Priya (spec + tests), Marco (infra + KMS), Taylor (migration + customers), Jamie (runbook + metrics). I'll update PRD with owners and change the scope matrix to MVS / Phase 2 / Phase 3. Please review before EOD :hourglass_flowing_sand:.

deploy-bot: PRD created: https://drive.redwood/prd/scoped-tokens?version=1.0; shard-check OK.

Taylor (solutions): :thumbsup: I'll consolidate customer asks into the PRD and mark 2 pilot customers for canary.

Alex (PM): Great. Follow-ups: Priya — could you paste the token schema snippet in the thread when you have 5 min?
